{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_014VZC6gmLjVWVF48Pti5Equ","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n2\t\n3\tResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\n4\tstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n5\t`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n6\t\n7\tEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\n8\trule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\n9\tnames a concrete type.\n10\t\"\"\"\n11\t\n12\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n13\t\n14\tfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\n15\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n16\t\n17\tfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\n18\tfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n19\t\n20\tTAB_STOP = 4\n21\tSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n22\t\n23\t# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n24\t# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\n25\tStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n26\t# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n27\t# when it returns True.\n28\tContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n29\t# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\n30\tAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n31\t# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\n32\tFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n33\t\n34\t\n35\tdef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n36\t    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n37\t    if char == \"\\t\":\n38\t        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n39\t    return col + 1\n40\t\n41\t\n42\tdef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n43\t    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n44\t    end = pos\n45\t    end_col = col\n46\t    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n47\t        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n48\t        end += 1\n49\t    return end_col - col\n50\t\n51\t\n52\tclass Cursor:\n53\t    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n54\t\n55\t    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n56\t        self.line = line\n57\t        self.pos = 0\n58\t        self.col = 0\n59\t\n60\t    @property\n61\t    def rest(self) -> str:\n62\t        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n63\t        return self.line[self.pos :]\n64\t\n65\t    @property\n66\t    def indent(self) -> int:\n67\t        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n68\t        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n69\t\n70\t    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n71\t        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n72\t        end = self.pos\n73\t        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n74\t            end += 1\n75\t        return end\n76\t\n77\t    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n78\t        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n79\t        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n80\t\n81\t    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n82\t        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n83\t        while self.pos < index:\n84\t            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n85\t            self.pos += 1\n86\t\n87\t    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n88\t        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n89\t        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n90\t\n91\t    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n92\t        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n93\t\n94\t        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n95\t        \"\"\"\n96\t        target = self.col + columns\n97\t        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n98\t            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n99\t            self.pos += 1\n100\t\n101\t\n102\tclass Block:\n103\t    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n104\t\n105\t    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n106\t        self.kind = kind\n107\t        self.parent: Block | None = None\n108\t        self.children: list[Block] = []\n109\t        self.is_open = True\n110\t        self.lines: list[str] = []\n111\t        self.content = \"\"\n112\t        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n113\t        self.level = 0\n114\t        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n115\t        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n116\t        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n117\t        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n118\t\n119\t    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n120\t        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n121\t        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n122\t            return self.children[-1]\n123\t        return None\n124\t\n125\t\n126\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n127\tclass BlockType:\n128\t    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n129\t\n130\t    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n131\t    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n132\t    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n133\t    \"\"\"\n134\t\n135\t    name: str\n136\t    continues: ContinueRule\n137\t    is_container: bool = False\n138\t    accepts_lines: bool = False\n139\t    interruptible: bool = False\n140\t    lazy: bool = False\n141\t    start: StartRule | None = None\n142\t    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n143\t    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n144\t\n145\t    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n146\t        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n147\t            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n148\t        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n149\t            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n150\t\n151\t\n152\tdef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n153\t    return True\n154\t\n155\t\n156\tdef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n157\t    return not cursor.is_blank()\n158\t\n159\t\n160\tdef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n161\t    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n162\t    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n163\t\n164\t\n165\tdef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n166\t    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n167\t\n168\t    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n169\t    \"\"\"\n170\t    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n171\t    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n172\t    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n173\t        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n174\t\n175\t\n176\tdef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n177\t    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n178\t    root = block\n179\t    while root.parent is not None:\n180\t        root = root.parent\n181\t    assert root.references is not None\n182\t    return root.references\n183\t\n184\t\n185\tdef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n186\t    return False\n187\t\n188\t\n189\tTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\n190\tTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n191\t\n192\t\n193\tdef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n194\t    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n195\t\n196\t    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n197\t    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n198\t    \"\"\"\n199\t    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n200\t        return None\n201\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n202\t    line = cursor.line\n203\t    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n204\t        return None\n205\t    marker = line[start]\n206\t    count = 0\n207\t    for char in line[start:]:\n208\t        if char == marker:\n209\t            count += 1\n210\t        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n211\t            return None\n212\t    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n213\t        return None\n214\t    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n215\t    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n216\t\n217\t\n218\tATX_MARKER = \"#\"\n219\tATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n220\t\n221\t\n222\tdef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n223\t    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n224\t\n225\t    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n226\t    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n227\t    \"\"\"\n228\t    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n229\t        return None\n230\t    line = cursor.line\n231\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n232\t    end = start\n233\t    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n234\t        end += 1\n235\t    level = end - start\n236\t    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n237\t        return None\n238\t    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n239\t        return None\n240\t    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n241\t    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n242\t    heading.level = level\n243\t    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n244\t    return heading\n245\t\n246\t\n247\tdef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n248\t    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n249\t\n250\t    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n251\t    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n252\t    \"\"\"\n253\t    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n254\t    if stripped == content:\n255\t        return content\n256\t    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n257\t        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n258\t    return content\n259\t\n260\t\n261\tDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\n262\tPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n263\t    \"paragraph\",\n264\t    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n265\t    accepts_lines=True,\n266\t    interruptible=True,\n267\t    lazy=True,\n268\t    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n269\t    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n270\t)\n271\t# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n272\t# as soon as the next line arrives.\n273\tTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n274\t    \"thematic_break\",\n275\t    continues=_never_continues,\n276\t    start=_thematic_break_start,\n277\t)\n278\t# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n279\t# inlines when the document is rendered.\n280\tATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n281\t    \"atx_heading\",\n282\t    continues=_never_continues,\n283\t    start=_atx_heading_start,\n284\t)\n285\t\n286\t\n287\tCODE_INDENT = 4\n288\t\n289\t\n290\tdef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n291\t    \"\"\"Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.\n292\t\n293\t    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and\n294\t    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph.\n295\t    \"\"\"\n296\t    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n297\t        return None\n298\t    cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n299\t    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n300\t\n301\t\n302\tdef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n303\t    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n304\t\n305\t    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n306\t    \"\"\"\n307\t    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n308\t        cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n309\t        return True\n310\t    return False\n311\t\n312\t\n313\tdef _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n314\t    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns.\"\"\"\n315\t    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n316\t\n317\t\n318\tdef _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n319\t    \"\"\"Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n320\t    lines = list(block.lines)\n321\t    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):\n322\t        lines.pop()\n323\t    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in lines)\n324\t\n325\t\n326\t# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n327\t# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.\n328\tINDENTED_CODE = BlockType(\n329\t    \"indented_code\",\n330\t    continues=_indented_code_continues,\n331\t    accepts_lines=True,\n332\t    start=_indented_code_start,\n333\t    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,\n334\t    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,\n335\t)\n336\t\n337\t\n338\tFENCE_CHARS = \"`~\"\n339\tFENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3\n340\tBACKTICK = \"`\"\n341\t\n342\t\n343\t@dataclass\n344\tclass Fence:\n345\t    \"\"\"The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.\n346\t\n347\t    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from\n348\t    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True\n349\t    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing\n350\t    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.\n351\t    \"\"\"\n352\t\n353\t    char: str\n354\t    length: int\n355\t    indent: int\n356\t    language: str\n357\t    opening: bool = True\n358\t    closed: bool = False\n359\t\n360\t\n361\tdef _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:\n362\t    \"\"\"Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`.\"\"\"\n363\t    end = start\n364\t    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:\n365\t        end += 1\n366\t    return end\n367\t\n368\t\n369\tdef _language(info: str) -> str:\n370\t    \"\"\"The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or \"\".\"\"\"\n371\t    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()\n372\t    return words[0] if words else \"\"\n373\t\n374\t\n375\tdef _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n376\t    \"\"\"Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.\n377\t\n378\t    The fence may be indented up to three columns. The info string is the rest of the line, trimmed.\n379\t    A backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence, so the line is left to the\n380\t    paragraph, where the backticks form a code span.\n381\t    \"\"\"\n382\t    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n383\t        return None\n384\t    line = cursor.line\n385\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n386\t    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in FENCE_CHARS:\n387\t        return None\n388\t    char = line[start]\n389\t    end = _run_end(line, start, char)\n390\t    if end - start < FENCE_MIN_LENGTH:\n391\t        return None\n392\t    info = line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n393\t    if char == BACKTICK and BACKTICK in info:\n394\t        return None\n395\t    fence = Fence(char=char, length=end - start, indent=cursor.indent, language=_language(info))\n396\t    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n397\t    block = Block(FENCED_CODE)\n398\t    block.fence = fence\n399\t    return block\n400\t\n401\t\n402\tdef _is_closing_fence(cursor: Cursor, fence: Fence) -> bool:\n403\t    \"\"\"True when the line is a closing fence for `fence`.\n404\t\n405\t    It uses the same character, is at least as long as the opening fence, is indented up to three\n406\t    columns, and is followed only by spaces or tabs.\n407\t    \"\"\"\n408\t    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n409\t        return False\n410\t    line = cursor.line\n411\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n412\t    end = _run_end(line, start, fence.char)\n413\t    return end - start >= fence.length and not line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n414\t\n415\t\n416\tdef _fenced_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n417\t    \"\"\"Every line continues the block except one after a closing fence.\n418\t\n419\t    A matching closing fence is consumed here and marked. Any other line loses up to the opening\n420\t    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.\n421\t    \"\"\"\n422\t    fence = block.fence\n423\t    assert fence is not None\n424\t    if fence.closed:\n425\t        return False\n426\t    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):\n427\t        fence.closed = True\n428\t        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n429\t        return True\n430\t    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)\n431\t    return True\n432\t\n433\t\n434\tdef _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n435\t    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of a content line. The opening and closing fence lines add nothing.\"\"\"\n436\t    fence = block.fence\n437\t    assert fence is not None\n438\t    if fence.opening:\n439\t        fence.opening = False\n440\t        return\n441\t    if fence.closed:\n442\t        return\n443\t    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n444\t\n445\t\n446\tdef _fenced_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n447\t    \"\"\"Join the content lines, each with a line ending, as the content.\n448\t\n449\t    An unclosed block keeps every line up to the end of its container.\n450\t    \"\"\"\n451\t    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in block.lines)\n452\t\n453\t\n454\t# A fenced code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n455\t# while it is open. It can interrupt a paragraph, because its start rule is tried in the paragraph's\n456\t# container.\n457\tFENCED_CODE = BlockType(\n458\t    \"fenced_code\",\n459\t    continues=_fenced_code_continues,\n460\t    accepts_lines=True,\n461\t    start=_fenced_code_start,\n462\t    add_line=_fenced_code_add_line,\n463\t    finalize=_fenced_code_finalize,\n464\t)\n465\t\n466\t\n467\tclass BlockRegistry:\n468\t    \"\"\"The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.\n469\t\n470\t    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no\n471\t    start rule matches a line of text.\n472\t    \"\"\"\n473\t\n474\t    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:\n475\t        self.root = root\n476\t        self.fallback = fallback\n477\t        self._names: set[str] = set()\n478\t        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []\n479\t        self.register(root)\n480\t        self.register(fallback)\n481\t\n482\t    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:\n483\t        \"\"\"Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order.\"\"\"\n484\t        if block_type.name in self._names:\n485\t            raise ValueError(f\"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}\")\n486\t        self._names.add(block_type.name)\n487\t        if block_type.start is not None:\n488\t            self._starts.append(block_type)\n489\t\n490\t    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:\n491\t        \"\"\"The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order.\"\"\"\n492\t        return tuple(self._starts)\n493\t\n494\t\n495\tDEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n496\tDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n497\tDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(ATX_HEADING)\n498\tDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(INDENTED_CODE)\n499\tDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(FENCED_CODE)\n500\t\n501\t\n502\tclass DocumentParser:\n503\t    \"\"\"Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time.\"\"\"\n504\t\n505\t    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:\n506\t        self.registry = registry\n507\t        self.root = Block(registry.root)\n508\t        self.root.references = ReferenceMap()\n509\t\n510\t    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:\n511\t        \"\"\"Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text.\"\"\"\n512\t        cursor = Cursor(line)\n513\t\n514\t        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.\n515\t        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)\n516\t        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None\n517\t\n518\t        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.\n519\t        started = False\n520\t        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n521\t            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n522\t            if new_block is None:\n523\t                break\n524\t            if not started:\n525\t                started = True\n526\t                all_closed = True\n527\t                self._close_below(container)\n528\t            self._attach(new_block, container)\n529\t            container = new_block\n530\t\n531\t        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n532\t        tip = self._tip()\n533\t        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n534\t            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n535\t            return\n536\t        self._close_below(container)\n537\t        if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n538\t            self._add_line(container, cursor)\n539\t        elif not cursor.is_blank():\n540\t            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n541\t            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n542\t            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n543\t\n544\t    def finish(self) -> Block:\n545\t        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n546\t        self._close_below(self.root)\n547\t        self.root.is_open = False\n548\t        return self.root\n549\t\n550\t    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n551\t        container = self.root\n552\t        while True:\n553\t            child = container.open_last_child()\n554\t            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n555\t                return container\n556\t            container = child\n557\t\n558\t    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n559\t        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n560\t            assert block_type.start is not None\n561\t            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)\n562\t            if new_block is not None:\n563\t                return new_block\n564\t        return None\n565\t\n566\t    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:\n567\t        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible\n568\t\n569\t    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:\n570\t        \"\"\"Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.\"\"\"\n571\t        while not container.kind.is_container:\n572\t            self._finalize(container)\n573\t            assert container.parent is not None\n574\t            container = container.parent\n575\t        container.children.append(new_block)\n576\t        new_block.parent = container\n577\t\n578\t    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n579\t        assert block.kind.add_line is not None\n580\t        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)\n581\t\n582\t    def _tip(self) -> Block:\n583\t        \"\"\"The deepest open block.\"\"\"\n584\t        tip = self.root\n585\t        while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None:\n586\t            tip = child\n587\t        return tip\n588\t\n589\t    def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None:\n590\t        child = container.open_last_child()\n591\t        if child is None:\n592\t            return\n593\t        self._close_below(child)\n594\t        self._finalize(child)\n595\t\n596\t    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:\n597\t        block.is_open = False\n598\t        if block.kind.finalize is not 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n# inlines when the document is rendered.\nATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"atx_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_atx_heading_start,\n)\n\n\nCODE_INDENT = 4\n\n\ndef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.\n\n    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and\n    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n\n    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns.\"\"\"\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n    lines = list(block.lines)\n    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):\n        lines.pop()\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in lines)\n\n\n# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.\nINDENTED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"indented_code\",\n    continues=_indented_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_indented_code_start,\n    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nFENCE_CHARS = \"`~\"\nFENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3\nBACKTICK = \"`\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.\n\n    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from\n    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True\n    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing\n    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    indent: int\n    language: str\n    opening: bool = True\n    closed: bool = False\n\n\ndef _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _language(info: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or \"\".\"\"\"\n    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()\n    return words[0] if words else \"\"\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.\n\n    The fence may be indented up to three columns. The info string is the rest of the line, trimmed.\n    A backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence, so the line is left to the\n    paragraph, where the backticks form a code span.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in FENCE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    char = line[start]\n    end = _run_end(line, start, char)\n    if end - start < FENCE_MIN_LENGTH:\n        return None\n    info = line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    if char == BACKTICK and BACKTICK in info:\n        return None\n    fence = Fence(char=char, length=end - start, indent=cursor.indent, language=_language(info))\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    block = Block(FENCED_CODE)\n    block.fence = fence\n    return block\n\n\ndef _is_closing_fence(cursor: Cursor, fence: Fence) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when the line is a closing fence for `fence`.\n\n    It uses the same character, is at least as long as the opening fence, is indented up to three\n    columns, and is followed only by spaces or tabs.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return False\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = _run_end(line, start, fence.char)\n    return end - start >= fence.length and not line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Every line continues the block except one after a closing fence.\n\n    A matching closing fence is consumed here and marked. Any other line loses up to the opening\n    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.\n    \"\"\"\n    fence = block.fence\n    assert fence is not None\n    if fence.closed:\n        return False\n    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):\n        fence.closed = True\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return True\n    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)\n    return True\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of a content line. The opening and closing fence lines add nothing.\"\"\"\n    fence = block.fence\n    assert fence is not None\n    if fence.opening:\n        fence.opening = False\n        return\n    if fence.closed:\n        return\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Join the content lines, each with a line ending, as the content.\n\n    An unclosed block keeps every line up to the end of its container.\n    \"\"\"\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in block.lines)\n\n\n# A fenced code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open. It can interrupt a paragraph, because its start rule is tried in the paragraph's\n# container.\nFENCED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"fenced_code\",\n    continues=_fenced_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_fenced_code_start,\n    add_line=_fenced_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_fenced_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nclass BlockRegistry:\n    \"\"\"The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.\n\n    Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no\n    start rule matches a line of text.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.root = root\n        self.fallback = fallback\n        self._names: set[str] = set()\n        self._starts: list[BlockType] = []\n        self.register(root)\n        self.register(fallback)\n\n    def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order.\"\"\"\n        if block_type.name in self._names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}\")\n        self._names.add(block_type.name)\n        if block_type.start is not None:\n            self._starts.append(block_type)\n\n    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order.\"\"\"\n        return tuple(self._starts)\n\n\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(ATX_HEADING)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(INDENTED_CODE)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(FENCED_CODE)\n\n\nclass DocumentParser:\n    \"\"\"Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:\n        self.registry = registry\n        self.root = Block(registry.root)\n        self.root.references = ReferenceMap()\n\n    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text.\"\"\"\n        cursor = Cursor(line)\n\n        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.\n        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)\n        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None\n\n        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds.\n        started = False\n        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is None:\n                break\n            if not started:\n                started = True\n                all_closed = True\n                self._close_below(container)\n            self._attach(new_block, container)\n            container = new_block\n\n        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n        tip = self._tip()\n        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n            return\n        self._close_below(container)\n        if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n            self._add_line(container, cursor)\n        elif not cursor.is_blank():\n            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n\n    def finish(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n        self._close_below(self.root)\n        self.root.is_open = False\n        return self.root\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n        container = self.root\n        while True:\n            child = container.open_last_child()\n            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n                return container\n            container = child\n\n    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n            assert block_type.start is not None\n            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is not None:\n                return new_block\n        return None\n\n    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:\n        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible\n\n    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.\"\"\"\n        while not container.kind.is_container:\n            self._finalize(container)\n            assert container.parent is not None\n            container = container.parent\n        container.children.append(new_block)\n        new_block.parent = container\n\n    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n        assert block.kind.add_line is not None\n        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)\n\n    def _tip(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"The deepest open block.\"\"\"\n        tip = self.root\n        while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None:\n            tip = child\n        return tip\n\n    def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None:\n        child = container.open_last_child()\n        if child is None:\n            return\n        self._close_below(child)\n        self._finalize(child)\n\n    def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None:\n        block.is_open = False\n        if block.kind.finalize is not None:\n            block.kind.finalize(block)\n\n\ndef parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> Block:\n    \"\"\"Build the block tree for `lines`, which hold no line-ending characters.\"\"\"\n    parser = DocumentParser(registry)\n    for line in lines:\n        parser.incorporate_line(line)\n    return parser.finish()\n","numLines":608,"startLine":1,"totalLines":608}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_014VZC6gmLjVWVF48Pti5Equ","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Ap5HisqoYPNefD7TrnqYEV","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n2\t\n3\tResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\n4\tpercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\n5\tentities must match the spec examples.\n6\t\"\"\"\n7\t\n8\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n9\t\n10\timport string\n11\tfrom collections.abc import Callable\n12\t\n13\tfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n14\t\n15\tInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n16\t\n17\tESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\n18\tURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\n19\tHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n20\t\n21\t\n22\tdef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n23\t    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n24\t    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n25\t        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n26\t    return text\n27\t\n28\t\n29\tdef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n30\t    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n31\t\n32\t    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n33\t    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n34\t    \"\"\"\n35\t    out: list[str] = []\n36\t    index = 0\n37\t    while index < len(url):\n38\t        char = url[index]\n39\t        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n40\t            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n41\t            index += 3\n42\t            continue\n43\t        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n44\t            out.append(char)\n45\t        else:\n46\t            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n47\t        index += 1\n48\t    return \"\".join(out)\n49\t\n50\t\n51\tdef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n52\t    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n53\t\n54\t\n55\tdef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n56\t    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n57\t\n58\t    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n59\t    returns that content's HTML.\n60\t    \"\"\"\n61\t    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n62\t\n63\t\n64\tdef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n65\t    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n66\t        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n67\t    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n68\t        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n69\t    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":\n70\t        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n71\t    if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":\n72\t        return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n73\t    if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":\n74\t        return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n75\t    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n76\t\n77\t\n78\tdef _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:\n79\t    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"\n80\t    assert block.fence is not None\n81\t    language = block.fence.language\n82\t    if not language:\n83\t        return \"<code>\"\n84\t    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'\n85\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"95afe858-f390-4c96-a94b-00c653ec1549","uuid":"efb9a7e2-94cd-4d6b-9875-f4116e64d17c","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:33:20.060Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/render.py","content":"\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":\n        return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":\n        return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    language = block.fence.language\n    if not language:\n        return \"<code>\"\n    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'\n","numLines":85,"startLine":1,"totalLines":85}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01Ap5HisqoYPNefD7TrnqYEV","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Diagnostics go to\n`sys.stderr` only, and the exit status is 0 for every input.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport sys\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks, inlines, render\n\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"�\"\nLINE_ENDING_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\r\\n|\\r|\\n\")\n\n\ndef decode_source(data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Decode raw input bytes as UTF-8, replacing each invalid byte with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    return data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n\n\ndef split_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Split text on LF, CR, or CRLF, and replace each U+0000 with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\x00\", REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER)\n    return LINE_ENDING_PATTERN.split(text)\n\n\ndef render_lines(lines: list[str]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Parse the lines into a block tree and return the HTML document.\n\n    A final line ending terminates the last line rather than starting an empty one, so the one empty\n    entry that `split_lines` leaves after it is dropped. Otherwise an unclosed fenced code block would\n    gain a blank line.\n    \"\"\"\n    if lines and lines[-1] == \"\":\n        lines = lines[:-1]\n    root = blocks.parse_lines(lines)\n    return render.render_document(root, lambda raw: inlines.parse_inline(raw, root.references))\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run the executable: stdin Markdown to stdout HTML. Always returns 0.\"\"\"\n    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()\n    try:\n        lines = split_lines(decode_source(data))\n        html = render_lines(lines)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"commonmark: internal error: {exc!r}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        html = \"\"\n    sys.stdout.buffer.write(html.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    sys.stdout.buffer.flush()\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n----\n\"\"\"Fenced code block tests: the seven declared checks from FEATURE-Fenced-Code.md, then block-tree and\nexact-output tests through the `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UFbjgLirzGhzm6HhYAMXMJ","type":"tool_result","content":"## HTML blocks\nAn [HTML block](@) is a group of lines that is treated\nas raw HTML (and will not be escaped in HTML output).\nThere are seven kinds of [HTML block], which can be defined by their\nstart and end conditions.  The block begins with a line that meets a\n[start condition](@) (after up to three optional spaces of indentation).\nIt ends with the first subsequent line that meets a matching\n[end condition](@), or the last line of the document, or the last line of\nthe [container block](#container-blocks) containing the current HTML\nblock, if no line is encountered that meets the [end condition].  If\nthe first line meets both the [start condition] and the [end\ncondition], the block will contain just that line.\n1.  **Start condition:**  line begins with the string `<pre`,\n`<script`, `<style`, or `<textarea` (case-insensitive), followed by a space,\na tab, the string `>`, or the end of the line.\\\n**End condition:**  line contains an end tag\n`</pre>`, `</script>`, `</style>`, or `</textarea>` (case-insensitive; it\nneed not match the start tag).\n2.  **Start condition:** line begins with the string `<!--`.\\\n**End condition:**  line contains the string `-->`.\n3.  **Start condition:** line begins with the string `<?`.\\\n**End condition:** line contains the string `?>`.\n4.  **Start condition:** line begins with the string `<!`\nfollowed by an ASCII letter.\\\n**End condition:** line contains the character `>`.\n5.  **Start condition:**  line begins with the string\n`<![CDATA[`.\\\n**End condition:** line contains the string `]]>`.\n6.  **Start condition:** line begins with the string `<` or `</`\nfollowed by one of the strings (case-insensitive) `address`,\n`article`, `aside`, `base`, `basefont`, `blockquote`, `body`,\n`caption`, `center`, `col`, `colgroup`, `dd`, `details`, `dialog`,\n`dir`, `div`, `dl`, `dt`, `fieldset`, `figcaption`, `figure`,\n`footer`, `form`, `frame`, `frameset`,\n`h1`, `h2`, `h3`, `h4`, `h5`, `h6`, `head`, `header`, `hr`,\n`html`, `iframe`, `legend`, `li`, `link`, `main`, `menu`, `menuitem`,\n`nav`, `noframes`, `ol`, `optgroup`, `option`, `p`, `param`,\n`search`, `section`, `summary`, `table`, `tbody`, `td`,\n`tfoot`, `th`, `thead`, `title`, `tr`, `track`, `ul`, followed\nby a space, a tab, the end of the line, the string `>`, or\nthe string `/>`.\\\n**End condition:** line is followed by a [blank line].\n7.  **Start condition:**  line begins with a complete [open tag]\n(with any [tag name] other than `pre`, `script`,\n`style`, or `textarea`) or a complete [closing tag],\nall on a single line, followed by zero or more spaces and tabs,\nfollowed by the end of the line.\\\n**End condition:** line is followed by a [blank line].\nHTML blocks continue until they are closed by their appropriate\n[end condition], or the last line of the document or other [container\nblock](#container-blocks).  This means any HTML **within an HTML\nblock** that might otherwise be recognised as a start condition will\nbe ignored by the parser and passed through as-is, without changing\nthe parser's state.\nFor instance, `<pre>` within an HTML block started by `<table>` will not affect\nthe parser state; as the HTML block was started in by start condition 6, it\nwill end at any blank line. This can be surprising:\n```````````````````````````````` example\n<table><tr><td>\n<pre>\n**Hello**,\n_world_.\n</pre>\n</td></tr></table>\n.\n<table><tr><td>\n<pre>\n**Hello**,\n<p><em>world</em>.\n</pre></p>\n</td></tr></table>\n````````````````````````````````\nIn this case, the HTML block is terminated by the blank line — the `**Hello**`\ntext remains verbatim — and regular parsing resumes, with a paragraph,\nemphasised `world` and inline and block HTML following.\nAll types of [HTML blocks] except type 7 may interrupt\na paragraph.  Blocks of type 7 cannot interrupt a paragraph.\n(This restriction is intended to prevent unwanted interpretation\nof long tags inside a wrapped paragraph as starting HTML blocks.)\nSome simple examples follow.  Here are some basic HTML blocks\nof type 6:\n```````````````````````````````` example\n<table>\n  <tr>\n    <td>\n           hi\n    </td>\n  </tr>\n</table>\nokay.\n.\n<table>\n  <tr>\n    <td>\n           hi\n    </td>\n  </tr>\n</table>\n<p>okay.</p>\n````````````````````````````````\n```````````````````````````````` example\n----\ntests/test_blocks.py:26:    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\ntests/test_blocks.py:207:    return [(child.kind.name, child.content) for child in root.children]\ntests/test_blocks.py:221:        registry.register(PARAGRAPH)\ntests/test_blocks.py:225:    assert blocks.DEFAULT_REGISTRY.starts() == (\ntests/test_blocks.py:243:# --- Extensibility: block types registered without changing the loop ---\ntests/test_blocks.py:256:def test_registered_start_rule_interrupts_a_paragraph() -> None:\ntests/test_blocks.py:258:    registry.register(RULE)\ntests/test_blocks.py:264:def test_registered_start_rule_closes_an_unmatched_block_before_it_starts() -> None:\ntests/test_blocks.py:266:    registry.register(RULE)\ntests/test_blocks.py:290:    registry.register(RAW)\ntests/test_blocks.py:291:    registry.register(RULE)\ntests/test_blocks.py:321:    registry.register(QUOTE)","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"95afe858-f390-4c96-a94b-00c653ec1549","uuid":"ea244fb8-858b-44dc-8cec-f2f1ef092caa","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:34:07.545Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"## HTML blocks\nAn [HTML block](@) is a group of lines that is treated\nas raw HTML (and will not be escaped in HTML output).\nThere are seven kinds of [HTML block], which can be defined by their\nstart and end conditions.
