Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n# inlines when the document is rendered.\nATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"atx_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_atx_heading_start,\n)\n\n\nCODE_INDENT = 4\n\n\ndef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.\n\n    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and\n    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n\n    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns.\"\"\"\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n    lines = list(block.lines)\n    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):\n        lines.pop()\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in lines)\n\n\n# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.\nINDENTED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"indented_code\",\n    continues=_indented_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_indented_code_start,\n    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nFENCE_CHARS = \"`~\"\nFENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3\nBACKTICK = \"`\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.\n\n    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from\n    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True\n    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing\n    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    indent: int\n    language: str\n    opening: bool = True\n    closed: bool = False\n\n\ndef _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _language(info: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or \"\".\"\"\"\n    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()\n    return words[0] if words else \"\"\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.\n\n    The fence may be indented up to three columns. The info string is the rest of the line, trimmed.\n    A backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence, so the line is left to the\n    paragraph, where the backticks form a code span.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in FENCE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    char = line[start]\n    end = _run_end(line, start, char)\n    if end - start < FENCE_MIN_LENGTH:\n        return None\n    info = line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    if char == BACKTICK and BACKTICK in info:\n        return None\n    fence = Fence(char=char, length=end - start, indent=cursor.indent, language=_language(info))\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    block = Block(FENCED_CODE)\n    block.fence = fence\n    return block\n\n\ndef _is_closing_fence(cursor: Cursor, fence: Fence) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when the line is a closing fence for `fence`.\n\n    It uses the same character, is at least as long as the opening fence, is indented up to three\n    columns, and is followed only by spaces or tabs.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return False\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = _run_end(line, start, fence.char)\n    return end - start >= fence.length and not line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Every line continues the block except one after a closing fence.\n\n    A matching closing fence is consumed here and marked. Any other line loses up to the opening\n    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.\n    \"\"\"\n    fence = block.fence\n    assert fence is not None\n    if fence.closed:\n        return False\n    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):\n        fence.closed = True\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return True\n    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)\n    return True\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of a content line. The opening and closing fence lines add nothing.\"\"\"\n    fence = block.fence\n    assert fence is not None\n    if fence.opening:\n        fence.opening = False\n        return\n    if fence.closed:\n        return\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Join the content lines, each with a line ending, as the content.\n\n    An unclosed block keeps every line up to the end of its container.\n    \"\"\"\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in block.lines)\n\n\n# A fenced code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open. It can interrupt a paragraph, because its start rule is tried in the paragraph's\n# container.\nFENCED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"fenced_code\",\n    continues=_fenced_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_fenced_code_start,\n    add_line=_fenced_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_fenced_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nHTML_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\nHTML_ATTRIBUTE = (\n    r\"[ \\t]+[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n    r\"(?:[ \\t]*=[ \\t]*(?:[^\\\"'=<>`\\x00-\\x20]+|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"))?\"\n)\n# A complete open tag or closing tag, with its name captured, as the raw HTML grammar defines it.\nCOMPLETE_OPEN_TAG = re.compile(rf\"<({HTML_TAG_NAME})(?:{HTML_ATTRIBUTE})*[ \\t]*/?>\")\nCOMPLETE_CLOSE_TAG = re.compile(rf\"</({HTML_TAG_NAME})[ \\t]*>\")\n# Start condition 1 names. Type 7 excludes them, because type 1 owns them.\nRAW_TEXT_TAG_NAMES = frozenset((\"pre\", \"script\", \"style\", \"textarea\"))\nRAW_TEXT_START = re.compile(r\"<(?:pre|script|style|textarea)(?=[ \\t>]|$)\", re.IGNORECASE)\nRAW_TEXT_END = re.compile(r\"</(?:pre|script|style|textarea)>\", re.IGNORECASE)\n# Start condition 6 names, matched case-insensitively.\nBLOCK_TAG_NAMES = (\n    \"address\", \"article\", \"aside\", \"base\", \"basefont\", \"blockquote\", \"body\", \"caption\", \"center\",\n    \"col\", \"colgroup\", \"dd\", \"details\", \"dialog\", \"dir\", \"div\", \"dl\", \"dt\", \"fieldset\", \"figcaption\",\n    \"figure\", \"footer\", \"form\", \"frame\", \"frameset\", \"h1\", \"h2\", \"h3\", \"h4\", \"h5\", \"h6\", \"head\",\n    \"header\", \"hr\", \"html\", \"iframe\", \"legend\", \"li\", \"link\", \"main\", \"menu\", \"menuitem\", \"nav\",\n    \"noframes\", \"ol\", \"optgroup\", \"option\", \"p\", \"param\", \"search\", \"section\", \"summary\", \"table\",\n    \"tbody\", \"td\", \"tfoot\", \"th\", \"thead\", \"title\", \"tr\", \"track\", \"ul\",\n)\nBLOCK_TAG_START = re.compile(\n    rf\"</?(?:{'|'.join(BLOCK_TAG_NAMES)})(?=[ \\t]|/?>|$)\", re.IGNORECASE\n)\nDECLARATION_START = re.compile(r\"<![A-Za-z]\")\n\n\ndef _prefix_test(pattern: re.Pattern[str]) -> HtmlStart:\n    \"\"\"A start test that holds when `pattern` matches at the start of the line text.\"\"\"\n    return lambda text: pattern.match(text) is not None\n\n\ndef _search_test(pattern: re.Pattern[str]) -> HtmlEnd:\n    \"\"\"An end test that holds when `pattern` matches anywhere in the line text.\"\"\"\n    return lambda text: pattern.search(text) is not None\n\n\ndef _contains_test(marker: str) -> HtmlEnd:\n    \"\"\"An end test that holds when `marker` appears anywhere in the line text.\"\"\"\n    return lambda text: marker in text\n\n\ndef _is_complete_tag_line(text: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when the line text is one complete open or closing tag, then spaces and tabs only.\n\n    The tag name may not be `pre`, `script`, `style` or `textarea`.\n    \"\"\"\n    match = COMPLETE_OPEN_TAG.fullmatch(text) or COMPLETE_CLOSE_TAG.fullmatch(text)\n    if match is None:\n        return False\n    return match.group(1).lower() not in RAW_TEXT_TAG_NAMES\n\n\nHtmlStart = Callable[[str], bool]\nHtmlEnd = Callable[[str], bool]\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass HtmlKind:\n    \"\"\"One of the seven HTML block types, given by its start test and end test.\n\n    `ends` is the end test for types 1 to 5, which is checked on each line. A line starts the first type whose start test holds.\nHTML_KINDS = (\n    HtmlKind(starts=_prefix_test(RAW_TEXT_START), ends=_search_test(RAW_TEXT_END)),\n    HtmlKind(starts=_prefix_test(re.compile(r\"<!--\")), ends=_contains_test(\"-->\")),\n    HtmlKind(starts=_prefix_test(re.compile(r\"<\\?\")), ends=_contains_test(\"?>\")),\n    HtmlKind(starts=_prefix_test(DECLARATION_START), ends=_contains_test(\">\")),\n    HtmlKind(starts=_prefix_test(re.compile(r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[\")), ends=_contains_test(\"]]>\")),\n    HtmlKind(starts=_prefix_test(BLOCK_TAG_START), ends=None),\n    HtmlKind(starts=_is_complete_tag_line, ends=None, can_interrupt=False),\n)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass HtmlState:\n    \"\"\"The start condition of an HTML block, and whether its end condition has been met.\n\n    `ended` is set when a line meets the end test of types 1 to 5. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"95afe858-f390-4c96-a94b-00c653ec1549","uuid":"e6a0de39-9a5d-4226-b926-fbe84046d8e7","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:37:37.268Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py","oldString":"DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(FENCED_CODE)\n","newString":"DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(FENCED_CODE)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(HTML_BLOCK)\n","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content already ends with a line ending.\n        return block.content\n    raise","originalFile":"\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":\n        return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":\n        return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    language = block.fence.language\n    if not language:\n        return \"<code>\"\n    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":72,"oldLines":6,"newStart":72,"newLines":9,"lines":["         return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"","     if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":","         return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"","+    if block.kind.name == \"html_block\":","+        # Raw lines pass through unchanged. Registry tests use block types defined here, which shows that\nthe loop never names a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks\nfrom mdparser.blocks import (\n    DOCUMENT,\n    PARAGRAPH,\n    Block,\n    BlockRegistry,\n    BlockType,\n    Cursor,\n    DocumentParser,\n    indent_columns,\n    next_column,\n    parse_lines,\n)\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_contents(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    return [child.content for child in block.children if child.kind is PARAGRAPH]\n\n\n# --- Column helpers ---\n\n\ndef test_next_column_for_a_space_advances_one() -> None:\n    assert next_column(\" \", 3) == 4\n\n\ndef test_next_column_for_a_tab_advances_to_next_tab_stop() -> None:\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 0) == 4\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 2) == 4\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 4) == 8\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_counts_spaces() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"   x\", 0, 0) == 3\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_expands_a_leading_tab_to_four() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\tx\", 0, 0) == 4\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_pads_a_tab_after_spaces_to_the_tab_stop() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"  \\tx\", 0, 0) == 4\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_counts_two_tabs_as_eight() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\t\\tx\", 0, 0) == 8\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_is_zero_without_leading_whitespace() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"x  \", 0, 0) == 0\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_starts_from_the_given_column() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\tx\", 0, 2) == 2\n\n\n# --- Cursor ---\n\n\ndef test_cursor_rest_starts_as_the_whole_line() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"abc\").rest == \"abc\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_is_blank_for_empty_and_whitespace_lines() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"\").is_blank()\n    assert Cursor(\" \\t \").is_blank()\n\n\ndef test_cursor_is_not_blank_with_text() -> None:\n    assert not Cursor(\"  a\").is_blank()\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_nonspace_tracks_column_across_a_tab() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"  \\t x\")\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    assert cursor.pos == 4\n    assert cursor.col == 5\n    assert cursor.rest == \"x\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_columns_consumes_whole_tab_when_it_overshoots() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"\\tx\")\n    cursor.advance_columns(2)\n    assert cursor.pos == 1\n    assert cursor.col == 4\n    assert cursor.rest == \"x\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_columns_stops_at_the_target_column() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"    x\")\n    cursor.advance_columns(2)\n    assert cursor.rest == \"  x\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_indent_reports_columns_to_next_text() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"\\t\\tx\").indent == 8\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_to_moves_by_characters() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"abc\")\n    cursor.advance_to(2)\n    assert cursor.rest == \"c\"\n\n\n# --- Empty and blank input ---\n\n\ndef test_empty_input_gives_empty_document() -> None:\n    assert parse_lines([]).children == []\n\n\ndef test_one_empty_line_gives_empty_document() -> None:\n    assert parse_lines([\"\"]).children == []\n\n\ndef test_blank_lines_only_give_empty_document() -> None:\n    assert parse_lines([\"\", \"  \", \"\\t\", \" \\t \"]).children == []\n\n\ndef test_leading_and_trailing_blank_lines_add_no_blocks() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"\", \" \", \"word\", \"\", \"\\t\", \"\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"word\"]\n\n\n# --- Paragraphs ---\n\n\ndef test_single_line_makes_one_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"hello\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"hello\"]\n\n\ndef test_blank_line_separates_paragraphs() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"one\", \"\", \"two\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"one\", \"two\"]\n\n\ndef test_repeated_blank_lines_separate_paragraphs_without_extra_blocks() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"one\", \"\", \"\", \"\", \"two\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\", \"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_consecutive_lines_stay_in_one_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"first\", \"second\", \"third\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"first\\nsecond\\nthird\"]\n\n\ndef test_continuation_lines_drop_their_leading_indentation() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"first\", \"      second\", \"\\tthird\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"first\\nsecond\\nthird\"]\n\n\ndef test_first_line_drops_leading_spaces() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"  word\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"word\"]\n\n\ndef test_final_spaces_and_tabs_are_removed_from_content() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"word \\t  \"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"word\"]\n\n\ndef test_trailing_spaces_on_an_interior_line_are_kept() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"foo  \", \"bar\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"foo  \\nbar\"]\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_is_closed_when_document_ends() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"word\"])\n    assert all(not child.is_open for child in root.children)\n    assert not root.is_open\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_is_closed_by_a_blank_line_before_the_next_one() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"one\", \"\", \"two\"])\n    assert [child.is_open for child in root.children] == [False, False]\n\n\ndef test_document_root_is_a_container_with_no_content() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"a\"])\n    assert root.kind is DOCUMENT\n    assert root.content == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_raw_lines_are_recorded_as_read() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"one\", \"   two\"])\n    assert root.children[0].lines == [\"one\", \"two\"]\n\n\ndef _shape(root: Block) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(child.kind.name, child.content) for child in root.children]\n\n\ndef test_parsing_the_same_lines_twice_gives_the_same_tree() -> None:\n    lines = [\"a\", \"\", \"b\", \"c\"]\n    assert _shape(parse_lines(lines)) == _shape(parse_lines(lines))\n\n\n# --- Registry ---\n\n\ndef test_registry_rejects_a_duplicate_block_type_name() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        registry.register(PARAGRAPH)\n\n\ndef blocks.ATX_HEADING,\n        blocks.INDENTED_CODE,\n        blocks.FENCED_CODE,\n    )\n\n\ndef test_lazy_block_type_must_accept_lines() -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1kJwmdNfRbuuLrDR76Z","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01NeThZDhNtEvopfLuuyu8By","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_html_blocks.py","content":"\"\"\"HTML block tests: the seven declared checks from FEATURE-HTML-Blocks.md, then block-tree and\nexact-output tests through the `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\nThe corpus section examples that use quotes, lists and indented code are gated in the tabs story\nand are not run here.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import HTML_BLOCK, Block, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef html_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[Block]:\n    \"\"\"The top-level HTML blocks that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child for child in parse_lines(lines).children if child.kind is HTML_BLOCK]\n\n\ndef html_contents(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The content of each top-level HTML block, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [block.content for block in html_blocks(lines)]\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-HTML-Blocks.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type6_raw_lines(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A block-level tag block passes through verbatim and its Markdown is not parsed.\"\"\"\n    block = \"<div>\\n*foo*\\n</div>\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, block + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert block in result.stdout\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type6_ends_at_blank_line(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A type 6 block ends at a blank line and Markdown after it is parsed.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"<div>\\nraw\\n\\n*bar*\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_comment_spans_blank_lines(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A comment block keeps blank lines until its end marker, and the following line is a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    comment = \"<!-- Foo\\n\\nbar\\n   baz -->\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, comment + \"\\nokay\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert comment in result.stdout\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_pre_spans_blank_lines(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A pre block keeps blank lines and does not parse the Markdown inside it.\"\"\"\n    block = \"<pre>\\n*x*\\n\\n_y_\\n</pre>\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, block + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert block in result.stdout\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type7_cannot_interrupt(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A lone open tag line after paragraph text stays inside the paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, 'Foo\\n<a href=\"bar\">\\nbaz\\n')\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type6_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A block-level tag line interrupts a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n<div>\\nbar\\n</div>\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_four_space_indent_is_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Four spaces of indentation make an indented code block, not an HTML block.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"    <!-- foo -->\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Start conditions ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"opener\", [\"<pre>\", \"<PRE>\", \"<script>\", \"<Style>\", \"<textarea>\", \"<pre class=\\\"x\\\">\"])\ndef test_type1_start_matches_each_raw_text_tag(opener: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Start condition 1 holds for pre, script, style and textarea in any case, and keeps blank lines.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([opener, \"*a*\", \"\", \"*b*\"]) == [\"html_block\", \"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type1_start_needs_a_space_tab_or_end_after_the_name() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<prefix` is not start condition 1, and it is not a complete tag either.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"<prefix\", \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type1_end_need_not_match_the_start_tag() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A script block ends at a style end tag.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<script>\", \"a\", \"</style>\", \"*b*\"]) == [\"<script>\\na\\n</style>\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type2_comment_start_and_end() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A comment block ends at the line that contains `-->`.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<!--\", \"a\", \"b -->\", \"*c*\"]) == [\"<!--\\na\\nb -->\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type2_start_needs_the_full_marker() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<!-x` is not a comment start.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"<!-x\", \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type3_processing_instruction_start_and_end() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A processing instruction block ends at the line that contains `?>`.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<?php\", \"a\", \"b ?>\", \"*c*\"]) == [\"<?php\\na\\nb ?>\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type4_declaration_ends_at_the_line_with_a_greater_than() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A declaration starts with `<!` and a letter, and its end line is the one with `>`.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<!DOCTYPE\", \"html>\", \"*c*\"]) == [\"<!DOCTYPE\\nhtml>\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type4_needs_a_letter_after_the_bang() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<!1` is not a declaration start.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"<!1x\", \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type5_cdata_start_and_end() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A CDATA block ends at the line that contains `]]>`.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<![CDATA[\", \"a\", \"b ]]>\", \"*c*\"]) == [\"<![CDATA[\\na\\nb ]]>\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type5_needs_the_full_cdata_marker() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<![CDATA` without its closing bracket is not a CDATA start.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"<![CDATA x\", \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"opener\", [\"<div>\", \"<DIV>\", \"<div/>\", \"<div class=\\\"x\\\">\", \"<div\\t>\", \"<p>\", \"</div>\"])\ndef test_type6_start_matches_block_tag_forms(opener: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Start condition 6 holds for an open or closing block tag followed by a space, tab, `>` or `/>`.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([opener, \"*a*\"]) == [\"html_block\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"opener\", [\"<divx\", \"<dix\", \"<pa\"])\ndef test_type6_start_needs_the_name_to_end_there(opener: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A block tag name followed by other letters is not start condition 6, and an incomplete tag is not type 7.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([opener, \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type6_ends_before_a_blank_line_and_the_blank_is_not_kept() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A type 6 block stops at the blank line, which is not part of its content.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<div>\", \"a\", \"\", \"*b*\"]) == [\"<div>\\na\\n\"]\n    assert kinds([\"<div>\", \"a\", \"\", \"*b*\"]) == [\"html_block\", \"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type6_blank_line_with_spaces_and_tabs_ends_the_block() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A line of only spaces and tabs is a blank line for ending a type 6 block.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"<div>\", \"  \\t \", \"*a*\"]) == [\"html_block\", \"paragraph\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"line\", ['<a href=\"bar\">', \"<a href='x' title=y data>\", \"<custom>  \", \"</a>\", \"<a/>\"])\ndef test_type7_start_matches_a_complete_tag_alone_on_its_line(line: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Start condition 7 holds for a complete open tag or closing tag, then spaces and tabs.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([line, \"*a*\"]) == [\"html_block\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"line\", ['<a href=\"x\"', \"<a> b\", \"<a></a>\", \"< a>\", \"<a b=>\"])\ndef test_type7_start_refuses_incomplete_or_trailing_content(line: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A tag that is not complete, or is followed by other text, is not start condition 7.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([line, \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type7_start_refuses_a_pre_tag_name_with_a_different_end() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<pre>` is start condition 1, so its block keeps going past the blank line instead of ending there.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<pre>\", \"*a*\", \"\", \"*b*\"]) == [\"<pre>\\n*a*\\n\\n*b*\\n\"]\n\n\n# --- Interruption of a paragraph ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"opener\", [\"<pre>\", \"<!--\", \"<?php\", \"<!DOCTYPE html>\", \"<![CDATA[\", \"<div>\"])\ndef test_types_1_to_6_interrupt_a_paragraph(opener: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Types 1 to 6 close an open paragraph and start an HTML block.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", opener, \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\", \"html_block\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"line\", [\"<custom>\", \"</custom>\", '<a href=\"b\">'])\ndef test_type7_cannot_interrupt_a_paragraph(line: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A complete tag line after paragraph text stays in the paragraph.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", line, \"baz\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type7_starts_after_a_blank_line_ends_the_paragraph() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Once a blank line closes the paragraph, type 7 can start a block.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"\", \"<custom>\", \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\", \"html_block\"]\n\n\n# --- End conditions and single-line blocks ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"line\",\n    [\"<pre></pre>\", \"<!-- x -->\", \"<? x ?>\", \"<!x>\", \"<![CDATA[x]]>\"],\n)\ndef test_types_1_to_5_on_one_line_make_a_single_line_block(line: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"When the first line meets both start and end conditions, the block is that line alone.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([line, \"*a*\"]) == [\"html_block\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert html_contents([line, \"*a*\"]) == [line + \"\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_types_1_to_5_end_line_keeps_text_after_the_end_tag() -> None:\n    \"\"\"The end line is part of the block, including anything after its end tag.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<pre>\", \"x</pre> tail\", \"*a*\"]) == [\"<pre>\\nx</pre> tail\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type1_block_runs_to_end_of_document_when_never_closed() -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unclosed type 1 block keeps every line to the end of the document, blank lines included.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<pre>\", \"a\", \"\", \"b\"]) == [\"<pre>\\na\\n\\nb\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type2_block_runs_to_end_of_document_when_never_closed() -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unclosed comment block keeps every line to the end of the document.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<!--\", \"a\", \"\", \"b\"]) == [\"<!--\\na\\n\\nb\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type6_block_at_end_of_document_has_no_trailing_blank_line() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A type 6 block with no following blank line ends at the end of the document.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<div>\", \"a\"]) == [\"<div>\\na\\n\"]\n\n\n# --- Raw lines and state ---\n\n\ndef The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\nThe corpus section examples that use quotes, lists and indented code are gated in the tabs story\nand are not run here.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import HTML_BLOCK, Block, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef html_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[Block]:\n    \"\"\"The top-level HTML blocks that of each top-level HTML block, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [block.content for block in html_blocks(lines)]\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-HTML-Blocks.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type6_raw_lines(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A block-level tag block passes through verbatim and its Markdown is not parsed.\"\"\"\n    block = \"<div>\\n*foo*\\n</div>\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, block + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert block in result.stdout\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type6_ends_at_blank_line(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A type 6 block ends at a blank line and Markdown after it is parsed.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"<div>\\nraw\\n\\n*bar*\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_comment_spans_blank_lines(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A comment block keeps blank lines until its end marker, and the following line is a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    comment = \"<!-- Foo\\n\\nbar\\n   baz -->\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, comment + \"\\nokay\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert comment in result.stdout\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_pre_spans_blank_lines(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A pre block keeps blank lines and does not parse the Markdown inside it.\"\"\"\n    block = \"<pre>\\n*x*\\n\\n_y_\\n</pre>\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, block + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert block in result.stdout\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type7_cannot_interrupt(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A lone open tag line after paragraph text stays inside the paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, 'Foo\\n<a href=\"bar\">\\nbaz\\n')\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type6_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A block-level tag line interrupts a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n<div>\\nbar\\n</div>\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_four_space_indent_is_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Four spaces of indentation make an indented code block, not an HTML block.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"    <!-- foo -->\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Start conditions ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"opener\", [\"<pre>\", \"<PRE>\", \"<script>\", \"<Style>\", \"<textarea>\", \"<pre class=\\\"x\\\">\"])\ndef test_type1_start_matches_each_raw_text_tag(opener: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Start condition 1 holds for pre, script, style and textarea in any case, and keeps blank lines.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([opener, \"*a*\", \"\", \"*b*\"]) == [\"html_block\", \"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type1_start_needs_a_space_tab_or_end_after_the_name() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<prefix` is not start condition 1, and it is not a complete tag either.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"<prefix\", \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type1_end_need_not_match_the_start_tag() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A script block ends at a style end tag.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<script>\", \"a\", \"</style>\", \"*b*\"]) == [\"<script>\\na\\n</style>\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type2_comment_start_and_end() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A comment block ends at the line that contains `-->`.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<!--\", \"a\", \"b -->\", \"*c*\"]) == [\"<!--\\na\\nb -->\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type2_start_needs_the_full_marker() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<!-x` is not a comment start.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"<!-x\", \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type3_processing_instruction_start_and_end() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A processing instruction block ends at the line that contains `?>`.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<?php\", \"a\", \"b ?>\", \"*c*\"]) == [\"<?php\\na\\nb ?>\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type4_declaration_ends_at_the_line_with_a_greater_than() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A declaration starts with `<!` and a letter, and its end line is the one with `>`.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<!DOCTYPE\", \"html>\", \"*c*\"]) == [\"<!DOCTYPE\\nhtml>\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type4_needs_a_letter_after_the_bang() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<!1` is not a declaration start.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"<!1x\", \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type5_cdata_start_and_end() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A CDATA block ends at the line that contains `]]>`.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<![CDATA[\", \"a\", \"b ]]>\", \"*c*\"]) == [\"<![CDATA[\\na\\nb ]]>\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type5_needs_the_full_cdata_marker() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<![CDATA` without its closing bracket is not a CDATA start.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"<![CDATA x\", \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"opener\", [\"<div>\", \"<DIV>\", \"<div/>\", \"<div class=\\\"x\\\">\", \"<div\\t>\", \"<p>\", \"</div>\"])\ndef test_type6_start_matches_block_tag_forms(opener: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Start condition 6 holds for an open or closing block tag followed by a space, tab, `>` or `/>`.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([opener, \"*a*\"]) == [\"html_block\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"opener\", [\"<divx\", \"<dix\", \"<pa\"])\ndef test_type6_start_needs_the_name_to_end_there(opener: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A block tag name followed by other letters is not start condition 6, and an incomplete tag is not type 7.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([opener, \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type6_ends_before_a_blank_line_and_the_blank_is_not_kept() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A type 6 block stops at the blank line, which is not part of its content.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<div>\", \"a\", \"\", \"*b*\"]) == [\"<div>\\na\\n\"]\n    assert kinds([\"<div>\", \"a\", \"\", \"*b*\"]) == [\"html_block\", \"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type6_blank_line_with_spaces_and_tabs_ends_the_block() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A line of only spaces and tabs is a blank line for ending a type 6 block.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"<div>\", \"  \\t \", \"*a*\"]) == [\"html_block\", \"paragraph\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"line\", ['<a href=\"bar\">', \"<a href='x' title=y data>\", \"<custom>  \", \"</a>\", \"<a/>\"])\ndef test_type7_start_matches_a_complete_tag_alone_on_its_line(line: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Start condition 7 holds for a complete open tag or closing tag, then spaces and tabs.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([line, \"*a*\"]) == [\"html_block\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"line\", ['<a href=\"x\"', \"<a> b\", \"<a></a>\", \"< a>\", \"<a b=>\"])\ndef test_type7_start_refuses_incomplete_or_trailing_content(line: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A tag that is not complete, or is followed by other text, is not start condition 7.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([line, \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type7_start_refuses_a_pre_tag_name_with_a_different_end() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<pre>` is start condition 1, so its block keeps going past the ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"opener\", [\"<pre>\", \"<!--\", \"<?php\", \"<!DOCTYPE html>\", \"<![CDATA[\", \"<div>\"])\ndef test_types_1_to_6_interrupt_a_paragraph(opener: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Types 1 to 6 close an open paragraph and start an HTML block.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", opener, \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\", \"html_block\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"line\", assert kinds([\"Foo\", line, \"baz\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type7_starts_after_a_blank_line_ends_the_paragraph() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Once a blank line closes the paragraph, type 7 can   \"line\",\n    [\"<pre></pre>\", \"<!-- x -->\", \"<? x ?>\", \"<!x>\", \"<![CDATA[x]]>\"],\n)\ndef test_types_1_to_5_on_one_line_make_a_single_line_block(line: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"When the [line + \"\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_types_1_to_5_end_line_keeps_text_after_the_end_tag() -> None:\n    \"\"\"The end line is part of the block, including anything after its end tag.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<pre>\", \"x</pre> tail\", \"*a*\"]) == [\"<pre>\\nx</pre> tail\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_type1_block_runs_to_end_of_document_when_never_closed() -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unclosed type 1 test_type2_block_runs_to_end_of_document_when_never_closed() -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unclosed comment block keeps every line to the end of the document.\"\"\"\n    assert html_contents([\"<!--\", source = \"<div>\\n*a* & <b>\\n</div>\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout == \"<div>\\n*a* & <b>\\n</div>\\n\"\n\n\ndef in the tabs story\nand are not run here.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import HTML_BLOCK, Block, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child for child in parse_lines(lines).children if child.kind is HTML_BLOCK]\n\n\ndef html_contents(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The content of each top-level HTML block, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [block.content for block in html_blocks(lines)]\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-HTML-Blocks.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type6_raw_lines(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A block-level tag block passes through verbatim and its Markdown is not parsed.\"\"\"\n    block = \"<div>\\n*foo*\\n</div>\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, block + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert block in result.stdout\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type6_ends_at_blank_line(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A type 6 block ends at a blank line and Markdown after it is parsed.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"<div>\\nraw\\n\\n*bar*\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_comment_spans_blank_lines(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A comment block keeps blank lines until its end marker, and the following line is a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    comment = \"<!-- Foo\\n\\nbar\\n   baz -->\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, comment + \"\\nokay\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert comment in result.stdout\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_pre_spans_blank_lines(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A pre block keeps blank lines and does not parse the Markdown inside it.\"\"\"\n    block = \"<pre>\\n*x*\\n\\n_y_\\n</pre>\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, block + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert block in result.stdout\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type7_cannot_interrupt(project_root: print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type6_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A block-level tag line interrupts a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n<div>\\nbar\\n</div>\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_four_space_indent_is_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Four spaces of indentation make an indented code block, not an HTML block.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"    <!-- foo -->\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Start conditions ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"opener\", [\"<pre>\", \"<PRE>\", \"<script>\", \"<Style>\", \"<textarea>\", \"<pre class=\\\"x\\\">\"])\ndef test_type1_start_matches_each_raw_text_tag(opener: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Start condition 1 holds for pre, script, style and textarea in any case, and keeps blank lines.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([opener, \"*a*\", \"\", \"*b*\"]) == [\"html_block\", \"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type1_start_needs_a_space_tab_or_end_after_the_name() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<prefix` is not start condition 1,  assert kinds([line, \"*a*\"]) == [\"html_block\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"line\", ['<a href=\"x\"', \"<a> b\", \"<a></a>\", \"< a>\", \"<a b=>\"])\ndef The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\nThe corpus section examples that use quotes, lists and indented code are gated in the tabs story\nand are not run here.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import HTML_BLOCK, Block, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef html_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[Block]:\n    \"\"\"The top-level HTML blocks that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child for child in parse_lines(lines).children if child.kind is HTML_BLOCK]\n\n\ndef html_contents(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The content of each top-level HTML block, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [block.content for block in html_blocks(lines)]\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-HTML-Blocks.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type6_raw_lines(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A block-level tag block passes through verbatim and its Markdown is not parsed.\"\"\"\n    block = \"<div>\\n*foo*\\n</div>\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, block + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert block in result.stdout\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type6_ends_at_blank_line(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A type 6 block ends at a blank line and Markdown after it is parsed.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"<div>\\nraw\\n\\n*bar*\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_comment_spans_blank_lines(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A comment block keeps blank lines until its end marker, and the following line is a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    comment = \"<!-- Foo\\n\\nbar\\n   baz -->\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, comment + \"\\nokay\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert comment in result.stdout\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_pre_spans_blank_lines(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A pre block keeps blank lines and does not parse the Markdown inside it.\"\"\"\n    block = \"<pre>\\n*x*\\n\\n_y_\\n</pre>\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, block + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert block in result.stdout\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type7_cannot_interrupt(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A lone open tag line after paragraph text stays inside the paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, 'Foo\\n<a href=\"bar\">\\nbaz\\n')\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_type6_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A block-level tag line interrupts a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n<div>\\nbar\\n</div>\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_htmlblock_four_space_indent_is_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Four spaces of indentation make an indented code block, not an HTML block.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"    <!-- foo -->\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Start conditions ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"opener\", [\"<pre>\", \"<PRE>\", \"<script>\", \"<Style>\", \"<textarea>\", \"<pre class=\\\"x\\\">\"])\ndef test_type1_start_matches_each_raw_text_tag(opener: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Start condition 1 holds for pre, script, style and textarea in any case, and keeps blank lines.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([opener, \"*a*\", \"\", \"*b*\"]) == [\"html_block\"]\n\n\ndef test_type1_start_needs_a_space_tab_or_end_after_the_name() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<prefix` is not start condition 1, and it is not a \"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type6_blank_line_with_spaces_and_tabs_ends_the_block() -> None:\n    \"\"\"A line of only spaces and tabs is a blank line for ending a type 6 block.\"\"\"\n    assert \"<a/>\"])\ndef test_type7_start_matches_a_complete_tag_alone_on_its_line(line: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Start condition 7 holds for a complete open tag or closing tag, then spaces and tabs.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([line, \"*a*\"]) == [\"html_block\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"line\", ['<a href=\"x\"', \"<a> b\", \"<a></a>\", \"< a>\", \"<a b=>\"])\ndef kinds([line, \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type7_start_refuses_a_pre_tag_name_with_a_different_end() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`<pre>` is start condition 1, so its block keeps going past the \"\"\"Types 1 to 6 close an open paragraph and start an HTML block.\"\"\"\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", opener, \"*a*\"]) == [\"paragraph\", \"html_block\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"line\", assert kinds([\"Foo\", line, \"baz\"]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_type7_starts_after_a_blank_line_ends_the_paragraph() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Once a blank line closes the paragraph, type 7 can
